covers.quote: Write the names of individual ships, aircraft and other vehicles:
Separate the names of vehicles from titles in citations and reference lists. Separate them according to the type of publication:
If the title is in italics (such as in book and website titles), use roman type for the name of the vehicle.
If the title is in roman type (such as a journal article), use italics for the name of the vehicle.

rules.violation_condition: An individual vehicle name is in roman type in ordinary text or within a roman-type citation title, or is italicised within an italicised citation title.
when: Applies to names of individual ships, aircraft and other vehicles, not brands, models, classes or generic types.
In ordinary text, use italics.
Within a citation or reference-list title, use roman type if the title is italicised, and italics if the title is in roman type.
Abbreviated ship-name prefixes are excluded from the italicised name.
A preceding definite article is included in the italicised name only when it is part of that name.
rules.why: G-1 separates italics from capitalisation; G-2 keeps citation-dependent type changes within the vehicle-name typography check.
